steps.text: Spread each slice of bread with 1 tablespoon cream cheese. On one slice of bread, arrange cucumber slices in a single layer. Cover with sprouts, then sprinkle with oil and vinegar. Layer tomato slices, lettuce, and pepperoncini. Spread other slice of bread with mashed avocado. Close sandwich and serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Cucumber Sandwich
raw_recipe.description: I worked at a sandwich shop that made these vegetable sandwiches stuffed with cucumbers, sprouts, tomatoes, and avocadoes. They were a veggie’s dream!
raw_recipe.name: Cucumber Sandwich

Cover with sprouts, then sprinkle with oil and vinegar. Layer tomato slices, lettuce, and pepperoncini. Spread other slice of bread with mashed avocado. Close sandwich and serve immediately.

review.reviewBody:
A great summertime sandwich! One of my favorites. I used pita bread, my husband prefers tortilla wraps. Pita bread can be a little messy but delicious. I also use low-fat cream cheese and just a couple slices of avocados. Two whole avodacos would be way too much (must be a misprint.)
Note to Eggyplant: a pepperoncini is a mild yellow pepper, also referred to as Banana Peppers. They are usually sold in jars near the pickle section. Gives the sandwich a little zing.

Really good sandwich! I mashed the avocado and then added the sliced pepperoncini to that and some garlic salt and pepper, and mixed it well. Used spinach, and lightly tossed the sprouts with red wine vinegar and sunflower seed oil before putting on the sandwich. I absolutely loved this sandwich!
Delicious! Didn't have cream cheese so I used Brie instead. I also added some French's fried onions and it was the perfect amount of a little salty and crunch.

I've made this twice now. The first time, I made no substitutions but after reading other reviews, did half the amount of olive oil and red wine vinegar. I had to agree with the review that said it just wasn't good. The taste of the olive oil was unpleasant for me. Also, it was very sloppy. The second time, I sharpened up my knife and sliced the veggies super-thin. That made a huge difference; the sandwich held together and was not sloppy at all. I also took another review into consideration and subbed Italian dressing for the oil and vinegar. Scrumptious! You actually had me at peperoncini and I thought I'd love the sandwich since I really love fresh-veggie sandwiches, and peperoncinis. I'm giving it four stars because even if I'd sliced the veggies thin the first time, the olive oil was off-putting and twice the amount of it would have wrecked it for me. Still a great base recipe though, and a great healthy option! Thanks!

Delicious! I didn't have pepperocini or romaine. I used spinach instead. I mashed 1 small avocado with about 1Tblsp chopped onion and garlic salt. I used Paul Neuman's balsamic dressing and toasted my multigrain wheat bread. It was very good.

I really enjoyed this sandwich! My husband, a meat lover, said he felt like he was eating a salad between two pieces of bread, nothing special. I tried bean sprouts since I could not find alfalfa, and I boiled the sprouts for one minute, adding the vinegar and olive oil to only the drained sprouts in an attempt to keep the sandwich from getting too soggy like other reviews had mentioned. The next day I took a sandwich for lunch and added a slice of Swiss cheese--delicious! We ate these sandwiches with a side of zucchini relish, a recipe I found on this site that was also very good.

Excellent, but kinda messy to eat. I made the sandwiches the second time using a baguette. Slice in half the long way, then pull out some of the bread so the halves are about 1/2 inch thick, creating a trough to put the ingredients in. Assemble and enjoy.

I loved this recipe. I made a little change to the cream cheese spread. I used 1 ounce of cream cheese, 1 Tbsp of mayonnaise and a little celery salt. Instead of a sandwich I made a wrap and it was perfect.

I’ve made a version of this sandwich for years and it is so delicious and refreshing! I usually put cream cheese on one slice of bread and mayonnaise on the other slice, don’t use oil and vinegar but do use salt and pepper on the veggies. I thinly slice the cucumbers and slice instead of mash avocado. I’ve also added chopped green olives to the cream cheese which is yummy. I will try also adding lettuce and banana peppers (I like those better than pepperocini) but don’t care for bean sprouts. Though my husband is a confirmed meat eater and hamburger lover he loves this vegetable sandwich!

This sandwich is sooo good! I have lost count how many times I have made it. I use 12 grain bread and for the tomatoes I used roma, but I can only fit 4 slices on the bread. For the cucumber I use the English style, so I did not have to peel it, saving time. I really liked the amount of vegetables on this and that it is sandwich shop qualty. I suggest using whipped cream cheese. It is not only lower in fat/sat fat, but it spreads much easier. The only thing I leave out is the sprouts, because I have never been able to find them. It doesn't seem to need them anyhow. It also tastes good with or without the yellow pepers. I make it both ways. I have found that "white wine" vinegar is much better to, as it is more mild. Thank you submitter!
Ok here comes the healthy nut. Instead of cream cheese I mashed 1/2 oz of goat cheese with just 1/4 of avocado and used that as my spread. Let me just say WOW! I'm in love. Thank you
OMG, it was so yummy! I used a plant based cream cheese and spinach instead of lettuce. I just had it for dinner tonight. 😀

I liked this very much. No changes made except to use whipped cream cheese because its easier to spread as another reviewer noted. The layer of cream cheese keeps the bread from absorbing the olive oil and vinegar and to my surprise was a delicious addition. I don't know why some reviews are saying the bread gets soggy, it shouldn't, because the recipe notes to eat immediately. Most enjoyable was after eating I didn't feel stuffed like I do when I eat a meat based sandwich.
Absolutely delicious! Left out the pepperoncini as husby can't do spice. Used the premashed Avocado individual pods (in this case, the one's from Trader Joe's). Great easy healthy recipe !
I love cucumber sandwiches. I didn’t have pepperoncini so I used mezzettas tamed jalapeños. And added a sprinkle of Everything Spice.

Loved it and loved the flavors. I never had an avocado and used balsamic vinegar instead of red wine but it was still great. I put it on sprouted bread and ate it for lunch for a couple days in a row. I think the vinegar and peppers are crucial and if you skip those then it won’t have much flavor

Delicious sandwich! Crunchy, creamy and so refreshing. I made this with my 11 yr old daughter and we both loved it! We added green peppers, red onion and oregano to the original recipe. Will be making this often!
I loved this sandwich! We have so many cucumbers in our garden and this was such a great way to use them. I highly recommend!
I didn’t have the sprouts and it still turned out good. Next time I will make it with sprouts.
We really liked it didn't have the the peppercini peppers at the time. Next time I will make sure I have some on hand. Definitely will make again.
